absences.what: The 1861 book sets this block across the full measure in English only and prints no Latin text for it; the facing-column Latin of every block that has one is transcribed. The absence is the witness's, not a rights or effort gap. It holds for 83 elements - 53 rubrics, 21 English headings, 8 prayers (a-cunctis, munda-cor-meum, dominus-sit-in-corde-meo, per-evangelica-dicta, accendat-in-nobis, secreta-ii, postcommunio-mundet, et-famulos) and the form benedicat-vos-omnipotens-deus - and each was established by opening the leaf, not inferred: leaves n25-n56 were all read. Some of these the 1962 Ordo Missae does print, accendat-in-nobis among them; the reason is scoped to this witness's page and says nothing about the rite.

advisory: A pre-1955 lay hand missal's Ordinary, and never a book to celebrate from. The English here is the anonymous translation an 1861 Philadelphia printing made for the laity to follow the Mass with; it is not an approved liturgical translation, it was never an altar book, and nothing in it may be used for recitation. It is carried under the 1962 Missal because the Ordinary is substantially the same rite, but it is a witness to the discipline in force before the 1955 and 1960 reforms, and it differs from the 1962 typical edition in orthography and in some rubrics. Where it prints something the 1962 Ordo Missae does not - a second collect, a second secret, devotions at the Gospel - the element says so in its own place. Both of the book's columns are now transcribed: the Latin named below is the 1861 printing's own, read from the facing column of the same openings, and it is a pre-1955 witness to the rite and never the text of the 1962 typical edition - its Communicantes prints no clause naming St Joseph, its Prefaces are the eleven this book knew, and its spelling, its j and its ae and oe ligatures are its own. Where the book sets a block across the full measure in English and prints no facing Latin at all, that silence is the witness's own and the element says so.
derived_from: Every element is read from a tab-separated artifact under edition.eugene-cummiskey.roman-missal-english-laity.philadelphia-1861, one row per printed block, transcribed visually from page images of the facsimile registered as that edition's ia-scan-pdf artifact at 640 dpi with doubtful characters re-read at 1600 dpi. The book's facing Latin column is transcribed in six sibling artifacts of the same edition, named on the sections below as artifact_latin, on the same division into printed blocks and joined to the English by element_key; they were read on 2026-08-20 from that item's own page images, and they carry a row only where the page prints facing Latin. Nothing about an element's order, kind, speaker, page or wording is restated in this file: it names the artifacts and the order they stand in, and the artifacts carry the words and the hashes.

elements.note: Italic across the full measure, with `Priest` in roman. DIFFERS FROM THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: there the words that follow are the priest's own, said silently while he kisses the book; here the assistants are directed to say them with him.

translations.text: Then they say with the Priest, in a low voice,

elements.note: Set to the full measure with no facing Latin. Speaker given as `all` because the book's own preceding rubric says the assistants say it with the Priest. The element key is taken from the received Latin incipit, which this page does not print.
elements.speaker: all

translations.text: May our sins be blotted out by the words of the Gospel.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure; `The` in ordinary upper and lower case, `NICENE CREED` in full capitals.

translations.text: The NICENE CREED.

elements.name: Credo in unum Deum Patrem
elements.note: The book prints no speaker for the Creed, so speaker is left empty. Two-line drop capital in both columns: C with REDO in capitals in the Latin, I with `Believe` in ordinary upper and lower case in the English, so the English drop capital is followed by a capitalised `Believe`, which is transcribed as printed.

translations.text: I Believe in one God, the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible.
CREDO in unum Deum Patrem omnipotentem, factorem cœli et terræ, visibilium omnium et invisibilium.

elements.latin_incipit: Et in unum Dominum Jesum Christum
elements.name: Et in unum Dominum Jesum Christum
elements.note: Runs over the page break at xxi/xxii, breaking in the English at `the Virgin` / `Mary` and in the Latin at `ex Maria Vir-` / `gine`. AND WAS MADE MAN is set in full capitals, matching the Latin ET HOMO FACTUS EST in the facing column; the asterisk after MAN. is the book's own and keys the footnote at the foot of xxii (see nota-incarnationis). Right-margin ink loss at the foot of xxi: `Virgin` prints with a damaged n reading almost as `Virgio`; read at 640 and 1600 dpi against the facing Latin `ex Maria Virgine`. The English renders `consubstantialem Patri` as `consubstantial to the Father`, not `with the Father`.

translations.text: And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son of God, and born of the Father before all ages. God of God; Light of Light; true God of true God; begotten not made; consubstantial to the Father, by whom all things were made. Who for us men, and for our salvation, came down from heaven, and became incarnate by the Holy Ghost of the Virgin Mary: AND WAS MADE MAN.* He was crucified also for us, suffered under Pontius Pilate, and was buried. And the third day he rose again according to the Scriptures. And ascended into heaven, sitteth at the right hand of the Father. And he is to come again with glory to judge both the living and the dead, of whose kingdom there shall be no end.

Et in unum Dominum Jesum Christum, Filium Dei unigenitum, et ex Patre natum ante omnia sæcula. Deum de Deo: Lumen de Lumine; Deum verum de Deo vero; genitum non factum; consubstantialem Patri, per quem omnia facta sunt. Qui propter nos homines, et propter nostram salutem descendit de cœlis. Et incarnatus est de Spiritu Sancto, ex Maria Virgine: ET HOMO FACTUS EST*. Crucifixus etiam pro nobis sub Pontio Pilato, passus et sepultus est. Et resurrexit tertia die secundum Scripturas. Et ascendit in cœlum, sedet ad dexteram Patris. Et iterum venturus est cum gloria judicare vivos et mortuos; cujus regni non erit finis.

elements.name: Et in Spiritum Sanctum, Dominum
elements.note: The facing Latin prints `qui ex Patre Filioque procedit`, so this printing DOES carry the Filioque, and the English renders it `who proceedeth from the Father and the Son`. The facing Latin prints `Et expecto resurrectionem mortuorum`, with expecto and NOT exspecto; read at 640 dpi in the lat-bot crop, where the word stands whole and unbroken at `Et expecto` on its own line. `Amen` in italic. A stray inked dot stands between `prophetas.` and `Et unam` in the Latin column.

translations.text: And in the Holy Ghost, the Lord and Giver of life, who proceedeth from the Father and the Son; who, together with the Father and the Son, is adored and glorified; who spoke by the prophets. And one holy Catholic and apostolic Church. I confess one baptism for the remission of sins. And I expect the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the world to come. Amen.

Et in Spiritum Sanctum, Dominum et vivificantem, qui ex Patre Filioque procedit: qui cum Patre et Filio simul adoratur, et conglorificatur; qui locutus est per prophetas. Et unam sanctam Catholicam et Apostolicam Ecclesiam. Confiteor unum Baptisma in remissionem peccatorum. Et expecto resurrectionem mortuorum, et vitam venturi sæculi. Amen.

elements.name: P. Dominus vobiscum
elements.note: Set in the facing columns immediately after the Creed. The `Oremus` that completes this greeting is carried over to the head of xxiii and is entered separately below.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: P. The Lord be with you. R. And with thy spirit.
P. Dominus vobiscum. R. Et cum spiritu tuo.

elements.note: NOT IN THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: a devotional footnote for the reader, not a rubric of the Ordo. Set in roman to the full measure at the foot of xxii, below the columns, keyed by the asterisk to AND WAS MADE MAN. in the Creed. Entered as kind rubric because the fixed vocabulary has no value for a footnote; it is a note, not a rubric of the rite.

translations.text: * At these words the assistants kneel down to adore God for the ineffable mystery of the incarnation.

elements.name: Oremus
elements.note: Italic in both columns, set as the first line of xxiii in the facing columns. No response is printed; it completes the greeting at the foot of xxii. Entered as kind dialogue for want of a closer value.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Let us pray.
Oremus.

elements.note: Italic across the full measure, turned over two lines; OFFERTORY in full capitals. The book prints no offertory antiphon text here.

translations.text: Here follows the OFFERTORY, which may be seen in its proper place.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure. OBLATION and HOST are in small capitals; `of the` is in italic upper and lower case.

translations.text: OBLATION of the HOST.

elements.latin_incipit: Suscipe, sancte Pater, omnipotens aeterne Deus
elements.name: Suscipe, sancte Pater, omnipotens aeterne Deus
elements.note: `Amen` in italic. A stray inked dot stands between `negligences,` and `and` in the English column; the comma itself is clear at 1600 dpi, so the mark is dirt and not punctuation. No cross sign is printed in either column.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Accept, O holy Father, almighty and eternal God, this unspotted Host, which I thy unworthy servant offer unto thee, my living and true God, for my innumerable sins, offences, and negligences, and for all here present; as also for all faithful Christians, both living and dead; that it may avail both me and them unto life everlasting. Amen.

Suscipe, sancte Pater, omnipotens æterne Deus, hanc immaculatam Hostiam, quam ego indignus famulus tuus offero tibi Deo meo vivo et vero, pro innumerabilibus peccatis, offensionibus et negligentiis meis, et pro omnibus circumstantibus; sed et pro omnibus fidelibus Christianis, vivis atque defunctis; ut mihi et illis proficiat ad salutem in vitam æternam. Amen.

elements.note: Italic across the full measure, turned over two lines, with `Priest`, `Wine`, `Water` and `Chalice` in a heavier italic. The book gives no blessing of the water and no `Deus qui humanae` cross sign.

translations.text: When the Priest puts the Wine and Water into the Chalice, he says,

elements.name: Deus qui humanae substantiae dignitatem
elements.note: `namely` and `Amen` in italic. The conclusion is abbreviated to `in the unity of, &c.` where the facing Latin sets it out in full to `per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.` Right-margin ink loss: `unity` prints as `unitj`, the y having lost its tail, and the closing `Amen.` is broken to `Anun.`; both read at 640 dpi against the facing Latin.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: O God, who, in creating human nature, hast wonderfully dignified it, and still more wonderfully reformed it: grant that by the mystery of this Water and Wine, we may be made partakers of his divine nature, who vouchsafed to become partaker of our human nature, namely, Jesus Christ our Lord thy Son, who with thee, in the unity of, &c. Amen.

Deus qui humanæ substantiæ dignitatem mirabiliter condidisti, et mirabilius reformasti; da nobis per hujus Aquæ et Vini Mysterium, ejus divinitatis esse consortes, qui humanitatis nostræ fieri dignatus est particeps, Jesus Christus Filius tuus Dominus noster: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate Spiritus sancti Deus; per omnia sæcula sæculorum. Amen.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure. OBLATION and CHALICE in small capitals, `of the` in italic upper and lower case.

translations.text: OBLATION of the CHALICE.

elements.name: Offerimus tibi, Domine, calicem salutaris
elements.note: `Amen` in italic. The facing Latin prints `calicem, salutaris,` with a comma after calicem, which is the printing's own error for `calicem salutaris`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: We offer unto thee, O Lord, the chalice of salvation, beseeching thy clemency: that it may ascend before thy divine Majesty, as a sweet odour, for our salvation, and for that of the whole world. Amen.
Offerimus tibi, Domine, calicem, salutaris, tuam deprecantes clementiam: ut in conspectu divinæ Majestatis tuæ, pro nostra et totius mundi salute cum odore suavitatis ascendat. Amen.

elements.note: Italic, centred across the full measure.

translations.text: When the Priest bows before the Altar, he says,

elements.latin_incipit: In spiritu humilitatis, et in animo
elements.name: In spiritu humilitatis, et in animo
elements.note: The book prints no Amen here, and the facing Latin ends at `Domine Deus.` The Latin sets `nodie` for `hodie`, the h having failed.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Accept us, O Lord, in the spirit of humility, and contrition of heart: and grant that the sacrifice we offer this day in thy sight, may be pleasing to thee, O Lord God.
In spiritu humilitatis, et in animo contrito suscipiamur a te, Domine: et sic fiat sacrificium nostrum in conspectu tuo nodie, ut placeat tibi, Domine Deus.

elements.note: Italic, centred across the full measure, with `Bread` and `Wine` in a heavier italic.

translations.text: When he blesses the Bread and Wine, he says,

elements.name: Veni, sanctificator, omnipotens aeterne Deus
elements.note: No cross sign is printed in either column, where the Latin rite prescribes one at `benedic`. The book prints no Amen.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Come, O almighty and eternal God, the sanctifier, and bless this sacrifice, prepared for the glory of thy holy name.
Veni, sanctificator, omnipotens æterne Deus, et benedic hoc sacrificium tuo sancto nomini præparatum.

elements.note: A full-measure horizontal rule is printed across both columns immediately above this rubric, marking off the solemn-Mass incensation matter that follows; the rule is the only one of its kind in this range. Italic, with `Masses` and `Incense` in a heavier italic.

translations.text: Here, in solemn Masses, he blesses the Incense, saying,

elements.name: Per intercessionem beati Michaelis archangeli
elements.note: The English conclusion is abbreviated to `Through,` with a comma and then `Amen.` in italic, where the facing Latin sets `Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.` in full. Both `Through,` and `Amen.` are undamaged at 640 dpi, so the comma is the printing's own.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: May the Lord, by the intercession of blessed Michael the archangel, standing at the right hand of the Altar of Incense, and of all his elect, vouchsafe to bless this incense, and receive it as an odour of sweetness. Through, Amen.

Per intercessionem beati Michaelis archangeli stantis a dexteris Altaris Incensi, et omnium electorum suorum, incensum istud dignetur Dominus benedicere, et in odorem suavitatis accipere. Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.

elements.note: Italic, centred across the full measure, with `Bread` and `Wine` in a heavier italic.

translations.text: At incensing the Bread and Wine, he says,

elements.name: Incensum istud a te benedictum
elements.note: `Incense` is capitalised in the English. The book prints no comma after `O Lord`; the line runs on within the measure, so this is not scan loss. No Amen.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: May this Incense which thou hast blest, O Lord ascend to thee, and may thy mercy descend upon us.
Incensum istud a te benedictum, ascendat ad te Domine, et descendat super nos misericordia tua.

elements.note: Italic across the full measure, with `Altar` in a heavier italic and the psalm citation `Ps. cxl.` in roman.

translations.text: At incensing the Altar, he says, Ps. cxl.

elements.name: Dirigatur, Domine, oratio mea
elements.note: The book prints no comma after the first `prayer`, putting it after `O Lord` instead; both words stand well inside the measure and are undamaged. The Latin `Dirigatur ... vespertinum` and `Pone Domine ... in peccatis` are set as one paragraph, and the English follows.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Let my prayer O Lord, be directed as incense in thy sight: the lifting up of my hands, as evening sacrifice. Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth: and a door of prudence around my lips; that my heart incline not to evil words to make excuses in sins.

Dirigatur, Domine, oratio mea, sicut incensum, in conspectu tuo: elevatio manuum mearum sacrificium vespertinum. Pone Domine custodiam ori meo, et ostium circumstantiæ labiis meis: ut non declinet cor meum in verba malitiæ, ad excusandas excusationes in peccatis.

elements.note: Italic across the full measure, with `Censer` and `Deacon` in a heavier italic. A stray inked mark stands immediately before `Deacon` in both the whole-page and the column renderings; it is dirt, not punctuation.

translations.text: On giving the Censer to the Deacon, he says,

elements.note: DIFFERS FROM THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE in presentation, not in substance: the prayer is in the 1962 Ordo, but this printing sets it to the FULL MEASURE with NO facing Latin at all, and drops the Amen. It is the only offertory prayer on xxiii-xxvi so treated. The element key is taken from the received Latin incipit, which the page does not print.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: May the Lord enkindle within us the fire of his love, and the flame of everlasting charity.

elements.note: Italic across the full measure, with `Hands` in a heavier italic and the psalm citation `Ps. xxv. 6.` in roman.

translations.text: Washing his Hands, he says, Ps. xxv. 6.

elements.name: Lavabo inter innocentes manus meas
elements.note: The Lavabo psalm is set as a run of separate printed paragraphs, one per verse, in both columns; each is entered here as its own row, following the book's own paragraphing.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: I will wash my hands among the innocent: and will compass thy altar, O Lord.
Lavabo inter innocentes manus meas: et circumdabo altare tuum, Domine.

elements.name: Ut audiam vocem laudis
elements.note: Right-margin ink loss: `the` at the end of the first line prints with a broken e, reading almost as `tho`; read against the facing Latin `Ut audiam vocem laudis`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: That I may hear the voice of thy praise: and tell all thy wondrous works.
Ut audiam vocem laudis: et enarrem universa mirabilia tua.

elements.name: Domine dilexi decorem domus tuae
elements.note: The book prints no comma after `loved`, following the Latin `Domine dilexi decorem`, which is also unpunctuated after `Domine`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: I have loved O Lord, the beauty of thy house, and the place where thy glory dwelleth.
Domine dilexi decorem domus tuæ, et locum habitationis gloriæ tuæ.

elements.latin_incipit: Ne perdas cum impiis animam meam
elements.name: Ne perdas cum impiis animam meam
elements.note: Runs over the page break at xxv/xxvi, breaking in the English at `with the wicked;` / `nor my life`. The signature `C` stands at the foot of xxv.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Take not away my soul, with the wicked; nor my life with bloody men.
Ne perdas cum impiis animam meam; et cum viris sanguinum vitam meam.

elements.name: In quorum manibus iniquitates sunt
elements.note: `right-hand` is hyphenated as printed.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: In whose hands are iniquities: their right-hand is filled with gifts.
In quorum manibus iniquitates sunt: dextera eorum repleta est muneribus.
But I have walked in my innocence: redeem me and have mercy on me.
Ego autem in innocentia mea ingressus sum: redime me, et miserere mei.
My foot hath stood in the direct way: in the churches I will bless thee, O Lord.
Pes meus stetit in directo: in ecclesiis benedicam te Domine.

elements.name: Gloria Patri, et Filio, &c.
elements.note: DIFFERS FROM THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: the doxology is abbreviated to its first words and `&c.` in both columns, where the Ordo Missae sets it out in full. The book prints no comma after `Father`, and no `Sicut erat` clause.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Glory be to the Father &c.
Gloria Patri, et Filio, &c.

elements.note: Italic, centred across the full measure, with `Altar` in a heavier italic.

translations.text: Bowing before the middle of the Altar, he says,

elements.name: Suscipe sancta Trinitas hanc oblationem
elements.note: Scan damage of the end-of-line hyphen kind the shared brief warns of: the English breaks `Re-` / `surrection` and the hyphen has been eaten, so the page as scanned reads `Passion, Re surrection`; the facing Latin breaks the same word at `Re-` / `surrectionis` with its hyphen intact, and controls the reading. `Amen` in italic. The English names `blessed Mary ever a virgin` and `blessed John Baptist`; the Latin conclusion is abbreviated to `Per eumdem, &c. Amen.` while the English sets it out as `Through the same Christ our Lord.`
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Receive O holy Trinity, this oblation which we make to thee in memory of the Passion, Resurrection, and Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in honour of the blessed Mary ever a virgin, of blessed John Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the Saints: that it may be available to their honour, and our salvation: and may they vouchsafe to intercede for us in heaven, whose memory we celebrate on earth. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

Suscipe sancta Trinitas hanc oblationem, quam tibi offerimus ob memoriam Passionis, Resurrectionis, et Ascensionis Jesu Christi Domini nostri: et in honorem beatæ Mariæ semper Virginis, et beati Joannis Baptistæ, et sanctorum Apostolorum Petri et Pauli, et istorum, et omnium Sanctorum: ut illis proficiat ad honorem, nobis autem ad salutem: et illi pro nobis intercedere dignentur in cœlis, quorum memoriam agimus in terris. Per eumdem, &c. Amen.

elements.note: Italic across the full measure, with `People` in a heavier italic. This is the first block on xxvii, a leaf that this project has not previously transcribed; the running head on it is PREFACES., not THE ORDINARY, and the signature `C 2` stands at its foot.

translations.text: Then turning himself towards the People, he says,

elements.latin_incipit: Orate Fratres: ut meum ac vestrum
elements.name: Orate Fratres: ut meum ac vestrum
elements.note: Neither column prefixes this block with `P.`, though the response that follows is prefixed `R.` in both. Right-margin ink loss on this leaf: `my` at the end of the first English line prints with a broken y; read against the facing Latin `ut meum ac vestrum sacrificium`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Brethren, pray that my sacrifice and yours may be acceptable to God the Father Almighty.
Orate Fratres: ut meum ac vestrum sacrificium acceptabile fiat apud Deum patrem omnipotentem.

elements.latin_incipit: R. Suscipiat Dominus sacrificium de manibus
elements.name: R. Suscipiat Dominus sacrificium de manibus
elements.note: The book prints NO comma after `name`, where the facing Latin has one after `nominis sui`; the terminal e of `name` is undamaged at 640 dpi, so the omission is the printing's own. The `R.` is printed in both columns and is kept in the English as the shared brief directs.
elements.speaker: server

translations.text: R. May the Lord receive the sacrifice from thy hands, to the praise and glory of his name to our benefit, and to that of all his holy Church.
R. Suscipiat Dominus sacrificium de manibus tuis ad laudem et gloriam nominis sui, ad utilitatem quoque nostram, totiusque Ecclesiæ suæ sanctæ.

elements.note: NOT IN THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: the seasonal second-Secret regime, matching the second-Collect rubric on xx. Italic across the full measure with roman for the emphasised words; SECRET in small capitals. `Candlemas-day` falls at a line break, so it cannot be settled whether the hyphen is the compound's own or the break's; the same book prints `Candlemas day` unhyphenated on xx. The opening parenthesis before `except` is printed without a closing space and the parenthesis is closed after `Octaves`.

translations.text: After reading the SECRET, which may be seen in its proper place, the second Secret from Candlemas-day, till Passion-Sunday and from the III. Sunday after Pentecost until Advent, (except on Doubles and within Octaves) is the following.

elements.note: NOT IN THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: a proper Secret printed bodily inside the Ordinary, the counterpart of the II. COLLECT on xx. Set to the FULL MEASURE with no facing Latin, so latin_incipit is empty. The label `II. SECRET.` is in roman capitals and is followed by an em rule, not a full stop and space. The element key is numbered from the printed label because the page prints no Latin incipit to derive one from. No conclusion is printed.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: II. SECRET.—Graciously hear us, O God our Saviour; that by virtue of this sacrament, thou mayest defend us from all enemies, of both soul and body: grant us grace in this life, and glory in the next.

elements.note: NOT IN THE 1962 ORDO MISSAE: the seasonal substitution rule for the second Secret. Italic with roman for the emphasised words; SECRET and SALVE in full capitals. The asterisk before `May` is printed on the page and has NO answering footnote anywhere on xxvii - the foot of the page carries only the signature `C 2` - so it stands unexplained. The book prints `&c,` with a comma, not `&c.` Note also `Low-Sunday, exclusively` here against `Low Sunday inclusively` in the matching collect rubric on xx.

translations.text: From Low-Sunday, exclusively, till the Ascension, instead of the foregoing is said the SECRET, * May, O Lord, &c, as in the Votive Mass, SALVE, of the B. V. M. p. 508.

elements.name: P. Per omnia saecula saeculorum
elements.note: Set in the facing columns; the Latin runs over two lines, `P. Per omnia saecula.` then `saeculorum. R. Amen.`, the full stop after `saecula` being the printing's own error. `Amen` in italic in both columns.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: P. World without end. R. Amen.
P. Per omnia sæcula. sæculorum. R. Amen.

elements.note: Centred in italic across the measure, above the dialogue. The common Preface itself begins on the following page and is outside this file.

translations.text: The Preface.

elements.name: P. Dominus vobiscum
elements.note: The whole Preface dialogue is set as one continuous block in each column, with the P. and R. run in. Scan damage of the end-of-line hyphen kind: the English breaks `lift-` / `ed` and the hyphen has been eaten, so the page as scanned reads `We have lift ed them up`; read against the facing Latin `R. Habemus ad Dominum.` and against the book's own unbroken usage. This is the last block on xxvii; `C 2` stands beneath it.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: P. The Lord be with you. R. And with thy spirit. P. Lift up your hearts. R. We have lifted them up to the Lord. P. Let us give thanks to the Lord our God. R. It is meet and just.
P. Dominus vobiscum. R. Et cum spiritu tuo. P. Sursum corda. R. Habemus ad Dominum. P. Gratias agamus Domino Deo nostro. R. Dignum et justum est.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure above both columns, in two lines. PREFACE is small capitals; the rest alternates italic and roman word by word: italic The, roman PREFACE, italic on, roman Festivals, italic and other Days that have none, roman proper, italic and in, roman Masses, italic for the, roman Dead. The running head over this page and over pp. xxix-xxxii is PREFACES. in small capitals, with the page number in the outer corner.

translations.text: The PREFACE on Festivals and other Days that have none proper, and in Masses for the Dead.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure between the heading and the columns; N. B. roman, the rest italic except the closing words proper Prefaces. which are roman. The asterisk is set close up to mark with no space. This note governs the whole apparatus of pp. xxviii-xxxii: no Latin heading is printed anywhere in this section, the headings are English and span both columns.

translations.text: N. B. This mark* refers to the subsequent part of the proper Prefaces.

elements.name: Vere dignum et justum est
elements.note: Two-line drop I in IT; the Latin column has the matching two-line drop V in VERE. HOW THE ASTERISK WORKS: the asterisk stands inside this common Preface at the seam, immediately before Thro' Christ our Lord (Latin * Per Christum Dominum nostrum), i.e. between eternal God. and Thro'. Every proper Preface on pp. xxviii-xxxii opens with an asterisk and is printed as the clause alone; the reader inserts it at this point, then resumes here at the second asterisk. A proper Preface that ends * Thro' &c. or * Per Christum, &c. or * By whom, &c. or * And, &c. resumes the common text at exactly this asterisk; one that ends with a dagger instead resumes at the conclusion of the Christmas Preface (see praefatio-de-nativitate). Scan damage: in seraphim the terminal m has broken strokes and reads seraphiin at 1600 dpi; read against the facing Latin seraphim and against the same word printed sound in the English column of p. xxix. The book uses French spacing, a thin space before colon and semicolon (agere : dicentes :); that spacing is not reproduced here.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: IT is truly meet and just, right and available to salvation, that we should always, and in all places, give thanks to thee, O holy Lord, Father Almighty, eternal God. * Thro' Christ our Lord: by whom the angels praise thy majesty, the dominations adore it, the powers tremble before it, the heavens, the heavenly virtues, and blessed seraphim, with common jubilee glorify it. Together with whom we beseech thee, that we may be admitted to join our humble voices, saying:

VERE dignum et justum est, æquum et salutare, nos tibi semper, et ubique gratias agere: Domine sancte, Pater omnipotens, æterne Deus. * Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Per quem majestatem tuam laudant angeli, adorant dominationes, tremunt potestates; Cœli cœlorumque virtutes, ac beata seraphim, socia exultatione concelebrant. Cum quibus et nostras voces, ut admitti jubeas deprecamur, supplici confessione dicentes:

elements.name: Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus, Dominus Deus
elements.note: Set as a separate indented paragraph after a blank line in both columns; the book prints no speaker attribution and no rubric over it. The Sanctus is printed ONCE only, here; it is never reprinted after any proper Preface, which are cued Holy, &c. in English and Sanctus, &c. in Latin.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth. Heaven and earth are full of thy glory. Hosanna in the highest. Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord, Hosanna in the highest.
Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus, Dominus Deus Sabaoth. Pleni sunt cœli et terra gloria tua. Hosanna in excelsis. Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini, Hosanna in excelsis.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure in two lines. TRINITY-SUNDAY in small capitals; On italic, and every other italic, Sunday roman, in the Year that has italic, no proper italic, Preface. roman.

translations.text: On TRINITY-SUNDAY, and every other Sunday in the Year that has no proper Preface.

elements.name: Qui cum unigenito Filio tuo
elements.note: The clause only, not a whole Preface: it opens with the asterisk and is inserted at the asterisk of praefatio-communis. Runs over the page break, breaking at art / one God between p. xxviii and p. xxix. No comma after one Lord, as printed. Scan damage at the right margin of p. xxix, all controlled at 1600 dpi against the facing Latin: believe of loses the f (prints as believe o, Latin hoc de Filio tuo); reveal- keeps only a blot where the hyphen was (revealed, Latin revelante); the end-of-line hyphen of Dei-ty is eaten entirely, the page printing Dei at the end of one line and ty, at the start of the next (Latin Deitatis); begotten at the foot of p. xxviii reads begotteu, the n having lost its right shoulder. The Latin column here prints Quam laudant angeli where the Roman text has Quem, and sets no full stop after æqualitas.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: * Who together with thy only begotten Son and the Holy Ghost, art one God, and one Lord not in a singularity of one Person, but in a Trinity of one substance. For what we believe of thy glory, as thou hast revealed, the same we believe of thy Son, and of the Holy Ghost, without any difference or distinction. So that in the confession of the true and eternal Deity, we adore a distinction in the Persons, an unity in the essence, and an equality in the Majesty. Whom the angels and archangels, the cherubim also and seraphim praise: and cease not daily to cry out with one voice saying, Holy, &c.

* Qui cum unigenito Filio tuo et Spiritu Sancto unus es Deus, unus es Dominus: non in unius singularitate Personæ, sed in unius Trinitate substantiæ. Quod enim de tua gloria, revelante te credimus, hoc de Filio tuo, hoc de Spiritu Sancto, sine differentia discretionis sentimus. Ut in confessione veræ, sempiternæque Deitatis, et in Personis proprietas, et in essentia Unitas, et in Majestate adoretur æqualitas Quam laudant angeli atque archangeli, cherubim quoque ac seraphim: qui non cessant clamare quotidie, una voce dicentes, Sanctus, &c.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure in two lines. CHRISTMAS-DAY in small capitals; From, till the, on, and on in italic, the rest roman. The book sets a thin space before the first semicolon (Epiphany ; on); not reproduced.

translations.text: From CHRISTMAS-DAY till the Epiphany; on Corpus Christi; and on our Lord's Transfiguration.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure between the heading and the columns, in two lines; N. B. Prefaces roman, the rest italic. The mark is an obelus (dagger) used as a reference mark, printed in the English column itself and so kept here; it is not a cross of blessing. Its force: a proper Preface whose text ends at a dagger takes the conclusion of THIS Christmas Preface from its dagger onward, i.e. And therefore with the angels and archangels ... saying, Holy, &c., instead of rejoining the common Preface at the asterisk.

translations.text: N. B. Prefaces thus marked † are concluded in the same manner as this.

elements.name: Quia per incarnati Verbi mysterium
elements.note: The clause plus a conclusion: asterisk at the head, dagger before And therefore. Not a whole Preface; the opening Vere dignum is not reprinted. Runs over the page break, breaking at with the / thrones between p. xxix and p. xxx. Scan damage: the end-of-line hyphen of everlast-ing is eaten entirely at the right margin of p. xxx, the page printing everlast at the end of one line and ing at the start of the next; read at 1600 dpi against the facing Latin hymnum gloriæ tuæ canimus. The hyphen of ap-peared is present but clipped. The Latin column of p. xxix has two broken sorts before invisibilium amorem where the Roman text reads in invisibilium amorem.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: * Since by the mystery of the Word made flesh, a new ray of thy glory has appeared to the eyes of our souls: that while we behold God visibly, we may be carried by him to the love of things invisible. † And therefore with the angels and archangels, with the thrones and dominations; and with all the heavenly host, we sing an everlasting hymn to thy glory, saying, Holy, &c.

* Quia per incarnati Verbi mysterium, nova mentis nostræ oculis lux tuæ claritatis infusit: ut dum visibiliter Deum cognoscimus per hunc in invisibilium amorem rapiamur. † Et ideo cum angelis et archangelis, cum thronis et dominationibus; cumque omni militia cœlestis exercitus, hymnum gloriæ tuæ canimus, sine fine dicentes, Sanctus, Sanctus, &c.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure on one line. No small capitals in this heading, unlike its neighbours: On the italic, Epiphany roman, and during its italic, Octave. roman.

translations.text: On the Epiphany and during its Octave.

elements.latin_incipit: Quia cum unigenitus tuus in substantia
elements.name: Quia cum unigenitus tuus in substantia
elements.note: The clause only; asterisk at the head, and the dagger cue at the end refers the reader to the conclusion of the Christmas Preface. The final line † And therefore, &c. is set flush left as a short line of its own, matching the Latin † Et ideo, &c.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: * Because when thy only begotten Son appeared in the substance of our mortal flesh, he repaired us by the new light of his immortality. † And therefore, &c.
* Quia cum unigenitus tuus in substantia nostræ mortalitatis apparuit, nova nos immortalitatis suæ luce reparavit. † Et ideo, &c.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure on one line. LENT in small capitals; In and till in italic, Passion-Sunday. roman.

translations.text: In LENT till Passion-Sunday.

elements.name: Qui corporali jejunio vitia comprimis
elements.note: The clause only. It closes with an asterisk, not a dagger, so it rejoins the common Preface: the English cue is * Thro' &c. with NO comma after Thro' (verified at 1600 dpi), where the parallel cue on the next Preface has one; the Latin cue is * Per Christum, &c.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: * Who by this bodily fast extinguishest our vices, elevatest our understanding, bestowest on us virtue and its reward. * Thro' &c.
* Qui corporali jejunio vitia comprimis, mentem elevas, virtutem largiris et præmia. * Per Christum, &c.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure in two lines. PASSION and PALM SUNDAYS in small capitals; On, and, and, of the in italic, the rest roman.

translations.text: On PASSION and PALM SUNDAYS, Maundy-Thursday, and Feasts of the Holy Cross.

elements.latin_incipit: Qui salutem humam generis in ligno
elements.name: Qui salutem humam generis in ligno
elements.note: The clause only; closes with an asterisk and so rejoins the common Preface, cue * Thro', &c. (with comma). Scan damage: man-kind is broken at the right margin but the hyphen survives. The Latin column prints humam generis for humani generis, a misprint of the book, verified at 1600 dpi; and closes Christum. &c. with a full stop where a comma is wanted. The latin_incipit above reproduces the misprint as printed.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: * Who hast appointed that the salvation of mankind should be wrought on the wood of the cross: that from whence death came, thence life might arise, and that he who overcame by the tree, might also by the tree be overcome. * Thro', &c.
* Qui salutem humam generis in ligno Crucis constituisti: ut unde mors oriebatur, inde vita resurgeret: et qui in ligno vincebat, in ligno quoque vinceretur. * Per Christum. &c.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure on one line. HOLY SATURDAY in small capitals; From and till the in italic, Ascension. roman.

translations.text: From HOLY SATURDAY till the Ascension.

elements.name: Vere dignum et justum est
elements.note: NOT a clause: this Preface is printed WHOLE, from Vere dignum, with the same two-line drop I and drop V as the common Preface, because its body differs from the common one. Runs over the page break, breaking at avail- / able between p. xxx and p. xxxi. DEFECT: the English column stops dead at † And at the foot of its last line and the Ascension heading follows immediately; therefore, &c. is simply not set, though the facing Latin closes † Et ideo, &c. Verified at 1600 dpi that nothing follows And and that no line has been lost to the gutter or the margin. Scan damage: after our death the comma has lost its tail and survives only as a dot below the line; read as a comma against the Latin destruxit, et vitam. The square brackets round night or day, or, at this time are the book's own, matching the Latin brackets round in hoc potissimum nocte vel die, vel; the opening Latin bracket has printed as a broken sort.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: IT is truly meet and just, right and available to salvation, to praise thee, O Lord, at all times, but chiefly on this [night or day, or, at this time] when Christ our Passover was sacrificed for us. For he is the true Lamb who hath taken away the sins of the world. Who by dying has destroyed our death, and by rising again has restored us to life. † And

VEre dignum et justum est, æquum et salutare, te quidem Domine omni tempore, sed [ in hoc potissimum nocte vel die, vel ] in hoc gloriosius prædicare, cum Pascha nostrum immolatus est Christus. Ipse enim verus est Agnus, qui abstulit peccata mundi. Qui mortem nostram moriendo destruxit, et vitam resurgendo reparavit. † Et ideo, &c.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure on one line. ASCENSION-DAY in small capitals; From and till in italic, Whitsun-Eve. roman.

translations.text: From ASCENSION-DAY till Whitsun-Eve.

elements.latin_incipit: Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Qui post
elements.name: Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Qui post
elements.note: The clause only. Note that here and in the Whitsuntide Preface the book spells the word out, Through Christ our Lord, where the common Preface and the Lent and Passion cues have Thro'. Ends at a dagger and so takes the Christmas conclusion.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: * Through Christ our Lord. Who after his resurrection appeared openly to all his disciples, and in their presence ascended into heaven, to make us partakers of his divine nature. † And therefore, &c.

* Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Qui post resurrectionem suam omnibus discipulis suis manifestus apparuit, et ipsis cernentibus est elevatus in cœlum, ut nos divinitatis suæ tribueret esse participes. † Et ideo, &c.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure in two lines. WHITSUN-EVE in small capitals; From, till, and in, of the in italic, the rest roman. In the word in of and in the i has lost its dot.

translations.text: From WHITSUN-EVE till Trinity-Sunday; and in Votive Masses of the Holy Ghost.

elements.latin_incipit: Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Qui ascendens
elements.name: Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Qui ascendens
elements.note: The clause with its own conclusion (no dagger; it runs on to saying, Holy, &c.). Runs over the page break, breaking at angelic pow- / ers between p. xxxi and p. xxxii. Square brackets round this day are the book's own, matching the Latin [hodierna die]. Scan damage at the right margin of p. xxxi, controlled at 1600 dpi against the facing Latin: the end-of-line hyphen of chil-dren is eaten entirely, the page printing chil at the end of one line and dren at the start of the next (Latin in filios adoptionis); in also the final o is clipped to a crescent (Latin Sed et supernæ virtutes). The book prints holy Spirit with a lower-case h.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: * Through Christ our Lord. Who ascending above all the heavens, and sitting at thy right hand, didst send down the promised holy Spirit [this day] upon the children of adoption. Wherefore the whole world displays its excess of joy. The heavenly virtues also and all the angelic powers, sing in concert an everlasting hymn to thy glory, saying, Holy, &c.

* Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Qui ascendens super omnes cœlos, sedensque ad dexteram tuam, promissum Spiritum sanctum [ hodierna die ] in filios adoptionis effudit. Quapropter profusis gaudiis totus in orbe terrarum mundus exultat. Sed et supernæ virtutes atque angelicæ potestates, hymnum gloriæ tuæ concinunt, sine fine dicentes, Sanctus, &c.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure in two lines. FESTIVALS and MARY in small capitals, B. V. in full capitals; On and of the in italic, and the parenthesis the Purification excepted. in italic. The full stop stands INSIDE the closing parenthesis, as printed.

translations.text: On FESTIVALS of the B. V. MARY (the Purification excepted.)

elements.latin_incipit: Et te in N. Beatæ Mariæ
elements.name: Et te in N. Beatæ Mariæ
elements.note: The clause only; closes with an asterisk and rejoins the common Preface, cue * By whom, &c. (Latin * Per quem, &c.). The mark after N. is a double dagger, printed in both columns and keyed to the footnote at the foot of the page; verified at 1600 dpi. Scan damage at the right margin: in and the the final e is clipped, in still the final l is thinned, and the hyphen of Vir-gin is raised and partly clipped; all read against the facing Latin Beatæ Mariæ semper Virginis / Virginitatis gloria permanente. The book sets a thin space before the colon in Son : and; not reproduced.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: * That we should praise, bless, and glorify thee on the N. ‡ of the blessed Mary, ever a Virgin. Who by the overshadowing of the Holy Ghost conceived thy only begotten Son: and the glory of her virginity still remaining, brought forth the eternal light of the world, Jesus Christ our Lord. * By whom, &c.

* Et te in N. ‡ Beatæ Mariæ semper Virginis colaudare, benedicere, et prædicare. Quæ et unigenitum tuum Sancti Spiritus obumbratione concepit: et Virginitatis gloria permanente, lumen æternum mundo effudit, Jesum Christum Dominum nostrum. * Per quem, &c.

elements.note: Centred across the full measure on one line. FESTIVALS and APOSTLES in small capitals; On the and of the in italic.

translations.text: On the FESTIVALS of the APOSTLES.

elements.name: Vere dignum et justum est
elements.note: NOT a clause: printed WHOLE from Vere dignum with the two-line drop I and drop V, like the Easter Preface, since its body replaces the common one; it nevertheless closes with an asterisk cue * And, &c. (Latin * Et ideo, &c.). No comma after thou, and none after Shepherd, as printed. A small raised mark stands after right in the second line; it matches no whole comma or apostrophe, the parallel opening on p. xxviii prints just, right and available with nothing after right, and it is read here as a broken sort or ink speck and not transcribed. This is the last block printed on p. xxxii apart from the footnote below; the next page opens THE CANON OF THE MASS.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: IT is truly meet and just, right and available to salvation, humbly to beseech thee that thou O Lord, our eternal Shepherd wouldst not forsake thy flock, but keep it under thy continual protection by thy blessed apostles. That it may be governed by those whom thou hast appointed its vicars and pastors. * And, &c.

VERE dignum et justum est, æquum et salutare, te Domine suppliciter exorare, ut gregem tuum Pastor æterne non deseras, sed per beatos apostolos tuos continua protectione custodias. Ut iisdem rectoribus gubernetur, quos operis tui vicarios eidem contulisti præesse pastores. * Et ideo, &c.

elements.note: Footnote set in italic across the full measure at the foot of the page, below both columns and below the Apostles Preface, separated by a blank line. It is keyed to the double dagger in the Preface of the Blessed Virgin. Its own leading mark is the double dagger.

translations.text: ‡ Here the Name of her several Festivals, as they occur in the course of the Year, should be expressed.

elements.note: Section head, set in even small capitals across the full measure above both columns.

translations.text: THE CANON OF THE MASS.

elements.name: Te igitur, clementissime Pater
elements.note: Two-line drop W. The book prints no cross signs anywhere in its English column; the three signs the Latin rite prescribes here are absent from both columns of this printing.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: WE therefore, humbly pray and beseech thee most merciful Father, thro' Jesus Christ thy Son, our Lord, that thou wouldst vouchsafe to accept and bless these gifts, these presents, these holy unspotted sacrifices, which in the first place we offer thee for thy holy Catholic Church, to which vouchsafe to grant peace; as also to preserve, unite, and govern it throughout the world: together with thy servant N. our pope N. our Bishop,

TE igitur, clementissime Pater, per Jesum Christum Filium tuum Dominum nostrum, supplices rogamus ac petimus, uti accepta habeas, et benedicas, hæc dona, hæc munera, hæc sancta sacrificia illibata, imprimis quæ tibi offerimus pro Ecclesia tua sancta catholica: quam pacificare, custodire, adunare, et regere digneris toto orbe terrarum: una cum famulo tuo Papa nostro N. et Antistite nostro N.

elements.name: et omnibus Orthodoxis
elements.note: The book sets this as a separate unindented block after the Bishop's N., matching the Latin column's own break at `et omnibus Orthodoxis`. Scan damage: `orthodox` prints as `ortnodox`, the h having lost its ascender; read at 1600 dpi and controlled against the facing Latin `Orthodoxis`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: as also all orthodox believers and professors of the catholic and apostolic Faith.
et omnibus Orthodoxis, atque Catholicæ et Apostolicæ Fidei Cultoribus.

elements.note: Set in small capitals across the full measure.

translations.text: COMMEMORATION OF THE LIVING.

elements.name: Memento Domine famulorum
elements.note: The book prints no comma after `mindful`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Be mindful O Lord of thy servants, men and women, N. and N.
Memento Domine famulorum famularumque tuarum N. et N.

elements.note: Italic, set across the full measure.

translations.text: He prays silently for those he intends to pray for.

elements.name: Et omnium circumstantium
elements.note: Runs over the page break at xxxiii/xxxiv. The book prints a full stop, not a comma, after `for whom we offer`, and sets a space before it; the lower-case `or` following is the book's own.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: And of all here present, whose Faith and Devotion is known unto thee, for whom we offer. or who offer up to thee this sacrifice of praise for themselves, their families, and friends: for the redemption of their souls, for the health and salvation they hope for, and for which they now pay their vows to thee, the eternal, living, and true God.

Et omnium circumstantium, quorum tibi fides cognita est, et nota devotio, pro quibus tibi offerimus: vel qui tibi offerunt hoc sacrificium laudis, pro se, suisque omnibus: pro redemptione animarum suarum, pro spe salutis et incolumitatis suæ: tibique reddunt vota sua æterno Deo, vivo et vero.

elements.name: Communicantes, et memoriam venerantes
elements.note: `COMMUNICATING` set in small capitals. This printing has NO clause naming Saint Joseph: it passes from `Jesus Christ` to `as also of the blessed Apostles`, the name having been inserted only by the decree of 13 November 1962. `Thadeus` is the book's spelling. Right-margin ink loss on this leaf: `by the`, `protection` and `Christ` each lose their last character; all three read against the facing Latin.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: COMMUNICATING with, and honouring in the first place, the memory of the ever glorious Virgin Mary, Mother of our Lord and God Jesus Christ: as also of the blessed Apostles and Martyrs, Peter and Paul, Andrew, James, John, Thomas, James, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon and Thadeus, Linus, Cletus, Clement, Xystus, Cornelius, Cyprian, Lawrence, Chrysogonus, John and Paul, Cosmas and Damian, and of all thy Saints; by whose merits and prayers grant that we may be always defended by the help of thy protection. Thro' the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

COMMUNICANTES, et memoriam venerantes, inprimis gloriosæ semper Virginis Mariæ, Genitricis Dei et Domini nostri Jesu Christi: sed et beatorum Apostolorum ac Martyrum tuorum, Petri et Pauli, Andreæ Jacobi, Joannis, Thomæ, Jacobi, Philippi, Bartholomæi, Matthæi, Simonis et Thadæi: Lini, Cleti, Clementis, Xysti, Cornelii, Cypriani, Laurentii, Chrysogoni, Joannis et Pauli, Cosmæ et Damiani, et omnium Sanctorum tuorum: quorum meritis precibusque concedas, ut in omnibus protectionis tuæ muniamur auxilio. Per eumdem Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.

elements.note: Italic.

translations.text: Spreading his Hands over the Oblation he says,

elements.name: Hanc igitur oblationem
elements.note: `We therefore` set in italic. Runs over the page break at xxxiv/xxxv. The conclusion is set out in full as `Through Christ our Lord`, not abbreviated to `Thro'` as the temporal orations of the same book usually are.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: We therefore beseech thee, O Lord, graciously to accept this oblation of our servitude, as also of thy whole family; dispose our days in thy peace, preserve us from eternal damnation, and rank us in the number of thine Elect. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

Hanc igitur oblationem servitutis nostræ, sed et cunctæ familiæ tuæ, quæsumus Domine, ut placatus accipias: diesque nostros in tua pace disponas, atque ab æterna damnatione nos eripi, et in Electorum tuorum jubeas grege numerari. Per Christum Dominum nostrum. — Amen.
Which oblation do thou, O God, vouchsafe in all respects, to bless, approve, ratify, and accept; that it may be made for us the body and blood of thy most beloved Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

Quam oblationem tu Deus in omnibus, quæsumus benedictam, adscriptam, ratam, rationabilem, acceptabilemque facere digneris; ut nobis Corpus et Sanguis fiat dilectissimi Filii tui Domini nostri Jesu Christi.

elements.name: Qui pridie quam pateretur
elements.note: Ends with a comma, the consecratory form following in the same paragraph.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Who the day before he suffered, took bread into his holy and venerable hands, and with his eyes lifted up towards heaven, giving thanks to thee, Almighty God, his Father; he blessed it, brake it, and gave it to his disciples, saying: Take and eat ye all of this,

Qui pridie quam pateretur, accepit panem in sanctas ac venerabiles manus suas, et elevatis oculis in cœlum, ad te Deum Patrem suum omnipotentem: tibi gratias agens, benedixit, fregit, deditque discipulis suis dicens: Accipite et manducate ex hoc omnes,

elements.name: Hoc est enim Corpus meum
elements.note: Set in small capitals, beginning at `FOR`. The Latin column sets `Hoc est enim Corpus meum` in the same small capitals and adds nothing after it: this printing has no counterpart to the postconciliar `quod pro vobis tradetur`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: FOR THIS IS MY BODY.
HOC EST ENIM CORPUS MEUM.

elements.note: Italic, set across the full measure and turned over two lines.

translations.text: After pronouncing the Words of Consecration, the Priest kneeling, adores and elevates the sacred Host.

elements.name: Simili modo postquam coenatum est
elements.note: Runs over the page break at xxxv/xxxvi.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: In like manner, after he had supped, taking also this excellent chalice into his holy and venerable hands, giving thee also thanks, he blessed, and gave it to his disciples, saying:
Simili modo postquam cœnatum est, accipiens et hunc præclarum calicem in sanctas ac venerabiles manus suas, item tibi gratias agens benedixit, deditque discipulis suis dicens:

elements.latin_incipit: Hic est enim Calix Sanguinis mei
elements.name: Hic est enim Calix Sanguinis mei
elements.note: Set in small capitals beginning at `TAKE`, so the caps extent differs from the form over the bread, which begins at `FOR`. `THE MYSTERY OF FAITH` stands INSIDE the form, as it does in the 1962 typical edition and as it does not in the 2002 Prex eucharistica I. Right-margin ink loss on this leaf: the hyphens of `CHA-LICE` and `MYS-TERY` are lost, `OF` after `MY BLOOD` loses its F, and `ETERNAL` loses its L; all read against the facing Latin.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: TAKE AND DRINK YE ALL OF THIS FOR THIS IS THE CHALICE OF MY BLOOD OF THE NEW AND ETERNAL TESTAMENT: THE MYSTERY OF FAITH: WHICH SHALL BE SHED FOR YOU, AND FOR MANY, TO THE REMISSION OF SINS.
ACCIPITE ET BIBITE EX EO OMNES, HIC EST ENIM CALIX SANGUINIS MEI NOVI ET ÆTERNI TESTAMENTI: MYSTERIUM FIDEI: QUI PRO VOBIS ET PRO MULTIS EFFUNDETUR IN REMISSIONEM PECCATORUM.

elements.name: Haec quotiescumque feceritis
elements.note: Printed as a separate paragraph after the form, not within it. Not in small capitals.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: As often as you do these things, ye shall do them in remembrance of me.
Hæc quotiescumque feceritis, in mei memoriam facietis.

elements.note: Italic, set across the full measure.

translations.text: Here also kneeling, he adores and elevates the Chalice.

elements.name: Unde et memores, Domine
elements.note: Right-margin dropout in `salvation`, which prints `salva.ion`; read against the facing Latin `Calicem salutis perpetuae`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Wherefore, O Lord, we thy servants, as also thy holy people, calling to mind the blessed passion of the same Christ thy Son our Lord, his resurrection from the dead, and admirable ascension into heaven, offer unto thy most excellent Majesty of thy gifts bestowed upon us, a pure Host, a holy Host, an unspotted Host, the holy bread of eternal life, and chalice of everlasting salvation.

Unde et memores, Domine, nos servi tui, sed et plebs tua sancta ejusdem Christi Filii tui, Domini nostri, tam beatæ passionis, necnon et ab inferis, Resurrectionis, sed et in Cœlos gloriosæ ascensionis, offerimus præclaræ Majestati tuæ, de tuis donis ac datis, Hostiam puram, Hostiam sanctam, Hostiam immaculatam, panem sanctum vitæ æternæ, et Calicem salutis perpetuæ.

elements.latin_incipit: Supra quae propitio ac sereno vultu
elements.name: Supra quae propitio ac sereno vultu
elements.note: Runs over the page break at xxxvi/xxxvii.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Upon which vouchsafe to look, with a propitious and serene countenance, and to accept them, as thou wert graciously pleased to accept the gifts of thy just servant Abel, and the sacrifice of our Patriarch Abraham, and that which thy High Priest Melchisedech offered to thee, a holy sacrifice and unspotted victim.

Supra quæ propitio ac sereno vultu respicere digneris, et accepta habere, sicuti accepta habere dignatus es munera pueri tui justi Abel, et sacrificium Patriarchæ nostri Abrahæ; et quod tibi obtulit summus sacerdos tuus Melchisedech, sanctum sacrificium, immaculatam Hostiam.

elements.name: Supplices te rogamus
elements.note: Runs over the page break at xxxvii/xxxviii. The conclusion renders `Per eumdem Christum` as `Thro' the same Christ`; the 2002 Prex eucharistica I drops `eundem` and parenthesises the whole conclusion.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: We most humbly beseech thee, Almighty God, command these things to be carried by the hands of thy holy angels to thy altar on high, in the sight of thy divine Majesty, that as many as shall partake of the most sacred body and blood of thy Son at this altar, may be filled with every heavenly grace and blessing. Thro' the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

Supplices te rogamus, omnipotens Deus, jube hæc præferri per manus sancti angeli tui in sublime altare tuum, in conspectu divinæ Majestatis tuæ, ut quotquot ex hac altaris participatione, sacro-sanctum Filii tui corpus et sanguinem sumpserimus, omni benedictione cælesti et gratia repleamur. Per eumdem Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.

elements.note: Set in small capitals across the full measure.

translations.text: COMMEMORATION OF THE DEAD.
Be mindful, O Lord, of thy servants N. and N. who are gone before us with the sign of Faith, and rest in the sleep of peace.
Memento etiam, Domine, famulorum famularumque tuarum N. et N. qui nos præcesserunt cum signo Fidei, et dormiunt in somno pacis.

elements.note: Italic, set across the full measure and turned over two lines.

translations.text: Here particular mention is silently made of such of the Dead as are to be prayed for.

elements.latin_incipit: Ipsis, Domine, et omnibus in Christo
elements.name: Ipsis, Domine, et omnibus in Christo
elements.note: Runs over the page break at xxxviii; the catchword `D` stands at the foot of xxxvii and the signature `D 2` at the foot of xxxix. The conclusion is set out in full and in lower case, `through`, where the same book abbreviates elsewhere.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: To these, O Lord, and to all that sleep in Christ grant, we beseech thee, a place of refreshment, light, and peace: through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
Ipsis, Domine, et omnibus in Christo quiescentibus, locum refrigerii, lucis et pacis, ut indulgeas deprecamur: per eumdem Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.

elements.note: Italic, set across the full measure.

translations.text: Here striking his Breast, the Priest says,

elements.name: Nobis quoque peccatoribus
elements.note: `Marcelline` and `Cecily` are the book's forms. The book prints NO Amen after this conclusion, as the 1962 typical edition also does not.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Also to us sinners, thy servants, confiding in the multitude of thy mercies, vouchsafe to grant some part and fellowship with thy holy apostles and martyrs; with John, Stephen, Matthias, Barnabas, Ignatius, Alexander, Marcelline, Peter, Felicitas, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucy, Agnes, Cecily, Anastasia, and with all thy saints: into whose company we beseech thee to admit us, not in consideration of our merit, but of thy own gratuitous pardon. Through Christ our Lord.

Nobis quoque peccatoribus famulis tuis de multitudine miserationum tuarum sperantibus, partem aliquam et societatem donare digneris, cum tuis sanctis apostolis et martyribus; cum Joanne, Stephano, Matthia, Barnaba, Ignatio, Alexandro, Marcellino, Petro, Felicitate, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucia, Agnete, Cæcilia, Anastasia, et omnibus sanctis tuis: intra quorum nos consortium, non æstimator meriti, sed veniæ, quæsumus largitor admitte. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.

elements.name: Per quem haec omnia, Domine
elements.note: The facing Latin prints `semper bona ereas` for `creas`, the c having failed; the English `create` is undamaged and controls the reading.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: By whom, O Lord, thou dost always create, sanctify, quicken, bless, and give us all these good things.
Per quem hæc omnia, Domine, semper bona ereas, sanctificas, vivificas, benedicis, et præstas nobis.

elements.latin_incipit: Per ipsum, et cum ipso, et in ipso
elements.name: Per ipsum, et cum ipso, et in ipso
elements.note: The book prints no full stop after `glory`; the sentence is completed by the following versicle at the head of xxxix. The five cross signs the Latin rite prescribes here are absent from both columns.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: By him and with him, and in him, is to thee, God the Father Almighty, in the unity of the Holy Ghost all honour and glory
Per ipsum, et cum ipso, et in ipso, est tibi Deo Patri omnipotenti, in unitate Spiritus Sancti, omnis honor et gloria.

elements.name: Per omnia saecula saeculorum
elements.note: The first two lines of xxxix, closing the Canon. The book's running head `THE CANON OF THE MASS` continues to xlii, over the Pater noster and the whole Communion rite, so the running head is not the boundary of the Canon.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: P. For ever and ever. R. Amen.
P. Per omnia sæcula sæculorum. R. Amen.

elements.name: Oremus
elements.note: Italic and centred in both columns, on the line immediately after the `Per omnia saecula saeculorum / R. Amen` versicle that closes the Canon. No response printed. Entered as kind dialogue for want of a closer value, following the same treatment given `Oremus` before the Offertory.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Let us pray.
Oremus.

elements.name: Præceptis salutaribus moniti
elements.note: Two-line drop B, the rest of the first word set `Eing`; the facing Latin has the matching two-line drop P with `Ræceptis`. Transcribed as the page prints it.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: BEing instructed by thy saving precepts, and following thy divine directions, we presume to say:
PRæceptis salutaribus moniti, et divina institutione formati, audemus dicere:

elements.latin_incipit: Pater noster, qui es in cœlis
elements.name: Pater noster, qui es in cœlis
elements.note: Set as one block in both columns with the response embedded, exactly as given here; `Amen.` is italic in both columns. The facing Latin prints `panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie` — QUOTIDIANUM with a `qu`, read at 1600 dpi and unambiguous; not `cotidianum`. The Latin also prints `dimittimus` and `tentationem`. Right margin sound on this leaf; no repairs needed.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name: thy kingdom come: thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven: give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive them that trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: R. But deliver us from evil. P. Amen.

Pater noster, qui es in cœlis, sanctificetur nomen tuum: adveniat regnum tuum: fiat voluntas tua sicut in cœlo, et in terra: panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie; et dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus debitoribus nostris: et ne nos inducas in tentationem: R. Sed libera nos a malo. P. Amen.

elements.name: Libera nos, quæsumus, Domine
elements.note: Runs over the page break at xxxix/xl, breaking within `disturb-ance`. `thro'` is the book's own contraction here while `Through` is set out in full four words later. No comma after `Mary`. This printing names only Peter, Paul and Andrew, and has no `and of all thy saints` clause beyond `and of all the saints`. Scan damage at the right margin of xl: the `t` of `Ghost` is blotted into the `s`, and the `d` of the closing `God` has lost the right of its bowl, leaving `Go` + ascender + full stop; both read at 1600 dpi against the facing Latin `Spiritus Sancti, Deus.` The book prints no cross sign in either column.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Deliver us, we beseech thee, O Lord, from all evils, past, present, and to come; and by the intercession of the blessed and ever glorious Virgin Mary Mother of God, and of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, and of Andrew, and of all the saints, mercifully grant peace in our days: that thro' the assistance of thy mercy, we may be always free from sin, and secure from all disturbance. Through the same Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, who with thee and the Holy Ghost liveth and reigneth, God.

Libera nos, quæsumus, Domine, ab omnibus malis, præteritis, præsentibus et futuris; et intercedente beata et gloriosa semper Virgine Dei Genitrice Maria, cum beatis apostolis tuis Petro et Paulo, atque Andrea, et omnibus sanctis, da propitius pacem in diebus nostris: ut ope misericordiæ tuæ adjuti, et a peccato simus semper liberi, et ab omni perturbatione securi. Per eumdem Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat, in unitate Spiritus Sancti, Deus.

elements.name: P. Per omnia sæcula sæculorum
elements.note: `Amen.` italic in both columns. Note that the identical Latin versicle at the head of xxxix is Englished `P. For ever and ever.` — the same formula is rendered two different ways eleven lines apart.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: P. World without end. R. Amen.
P. Per omnia sæcula sæculorum. R. Amen.

elements.latin_incipit: P. Pax Domini sit semper vobiscum
elements.name: P. Pax Domini sit semper vobiscum
elements.note: One block. The Latin column leaves a blank line before `R. Et cum spiritu tuo.` so that the response lines up with the third line of the English; the English sets the response immediately after `you.` The terminal `t` of `spirit.` is blotted into the stop but legible at 1600 dpi.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: P. May the peace of the Lord be always with you. R. And with thy spirit.
P. Pax Domini sit semper vobiscum. R. Et cum spiritu tuo.

elements.note: Set across the full measure, so there is no facing Latin at all: this printing gives the commixture prayer (Haec commixtio) in English only, embedded in its rubric. `Breaking the Host, he puts a Particle thereof into the Chalice saying,` and the closing `Amen.` are italic; the prayer between them is roman. Entered as kind rubric because the block opens and is governed as one; the roman part is the priest's prayer.

translations.text: Breaking the Host, he puts a Particle thereof into the Chalice saying, May this mixture, and consecration of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, be to us that receive it effectual to eternal life. Amen.

elements.note: Italic, centred on its own line across the full measure. Ends with a colon.

translations.text: Then bowing and striking his Breast, he says:

elements.latin_incipit: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi
elements.name: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi
elements.note: Three asterisks, marking where the invocation is resumed. The Latin column sets them at the head of three separate short lines (`* miserere nobis,` twice, then `* dona nobis pacem.`); the English runs them inline. The third petition reads exactly `* give us peace.` — not `grant us peace`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Lamb of God, who takest away the sins of the world, * have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us, * give us peace.
Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi, * miserere nobis, * miserere nobis, * dona nobis pacem.

elements.note: Full measure, turned over two lines. `DEAD` is set in small capitals; the small-capital run is that word only. Italic for `In Masses for the`, `he says twice,` and `and lastly,`; the quoted responses `Give them rest;` and `* Give them eternal rest.` are roman.

translations.text: In Masses for the DEAD he says twice, Give them rest; and lastly, * Give them eternal rest.

elements.note: Italic, centred on its own line across the full measure. `Prayer` capitalised.

translations.text: The following Prayer is then also omitted.

elements.name: Domine Jesu Christe, qui dixisti
elements.note: Runs over the page break at xl/xli. The English conclusion has no counterpart to the Latin's `Deus`: the Latin closes `qui vivis et regnas Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.` Heavy right-margin ink loss on xl, all read at 1600 dpi against the facing Latin: `who` prints with the ascender of its `h` eaten (`wr o`), read against `qui dixisti`; the `I` of `apostles, I` has lost its upper serif and stands as a bare stroke, read against `pacem relinquo vobis`; the `d` of `regard` has lost its bowl, read against `ne respicias peccata mea`. `church` is lower case in the book. The Latin column prints `.untatem` for `voluntatem`, its `vol-` having been broken across the line as `vo-`. On the carry-over line at the head of xli the `r` of `for ever` has lost its shoulder and prints as `foi`; mid-line, not at the margin, read at 1600 dpi against the Latin `per omnia saecula saeculorum`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Lord Jesus Christ, who saidst to thy apostles, I leave you peace, I give you my peace, regard not my sins, but the faith of thy church; and grant her that peace and unity which is agreeable to thy will: who livest and reignest for ever and ever. Amen.

Domine Jesu Christe, qui dixisti apostolis tuis, pacem relinquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis, ne respicias peccata mea, sed fidem Ecclesiæ tuæ; eamque secundum voluntatem tuam pacificare et coadunare digneris qui vivis et regnas Deus, per omnia sæcula sæculorum. Amen.

elements.latin_incipit: Domine Jesu Christe, Fili Dei vivi
elements.name: Domine Jesu Christe, Fili Dei vivi
elements.note: `co-operation` is broken as `co-ope-` / `ration`; the word's own hyphen is the one kept here. The conclusion is abbreviated `&c.` in the English while the Latin sets it out in full to `in saecula saeculorum`. No rubric separates this prayer from the one before it or from the one after.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who, according to the will of thy Father, hast by thy death, thro' the co-operation of the Holy Ghost, given life to the world, deliver me by this thy most sacred body and blood from all my iniquities, and from all evils; and make me always adhere to thy commandments, and never suffer me to be separated from thee: who livest and reignest with God the Father, &c. Amen.

Domine Jesu Christe, Fili Dei vivi, qui ex voluntate Patris, co-operante Spiritu Sancto, per mortem tuam mundum vivificasti, libera me per hoc sacro-sanctum corpus et sanguinem tuum ab omnibus iniquitatibus meis, et universis malis: et fac me tuis, semper inhærere mandatis, et a te nunquam separari permittas: qui cum eodem Deo Patre et Spiritu Sancto vivis et regnas Deus in sæcula sæculorum. Amen.

elements.name: Perceptio corporis tui, Domine
elements.note: The book sets a full space before the comma in `condemnation , but`; normalised here and noted, as elsewhere in this artifact. `safeguard` is broken `safe-` / `guard`. `judgment` without the medial `e`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Let not the participation of thy body, O Lord Jesus Christ, which I, though unworthy, presume to receive, turn to my judgment and condemnation, but thro' thy mercy, may it be a safeguard and remedy, both to soul and body; who with God the Father, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, livest and reignest God for ever and ever. Amen.

Perceptio corporis tui, Domine Jesu Christe, quod ego indignus sumere præsumo, non mihi proveniat in judicium et condemnationem; sed pro tua pietate prosit mihi ad tutamentum mentis et corporis, et ad medelam percipiendam: qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitate Spiritus Sancti, Deus, per omnia sæcula sæculorum. Amen.

elements.note: Italic, centred on its own line across the full measure, at the foot of xli.

translations.text: Taking the Host in his Hands, he says,

elements.name: Panem cœlestem accipiam
elements.note: Runs over the page break at xli/xlii, the Latin breaking within `ac-cipiam`. The English says `our Lord` where the Latin has `nomen Domini`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: I will take the bread of heaven, and call upon the name of our Lord.
Panem cœlestem accipiam, et nomen Domini invocabo.

elements.note: Italic, full measure, turned over two lines. This is the book's own statement that the following prayer is said three times; it prints the prayer once only.

translations.text: Striking his Breast, with Humility and Devotion, he says thrice,

elements.name: Domine, non sum dignus
elements.note: Printed once, under the rubric at row 17 that says it thrice. The capital `I` of `I am` has lost its upper-left serif and reads at first sight as a figure 1; read at 1600 dpi against the fully-serifed `I will` on the same page and against the Latin `non sum dignus`. The `r` of `enter` is thinned at the right margin but whole. There is no `Ecce Agnus Dei` and no Communion of the people anywhere on this opening.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof; say but the word, and my soul shall be healed.
Domine, non sum dignus ut intres sub tectum meum; sed tantum dic verbo, et sanabitur anima mea.

elements.note: Italic, centred on its own line across the full measure.

translations.text: Receiving reverently both Parts of the Host, he says,

elements.name: Corpus Domini nostri Jesu Christi
elements.note: `Amen.` italic in both columns. The book prints no cross sign in either column.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: May the body of our Lord Jesus Christ preserve my soul to life everlasting. Amen.
Corpus Domini nostri Jesu Christi custodiat animam meam in vitam æternam. Amen.

elements.note: Italic, centred on its own line across the full measure.

translations.text: Taking the Chalice, he says,

elements.name: Quid retribuam Domino
elements.note: The book sets a space before the question mark in `to me ?`; normalised here and noted. `Chalice` capitalised in the English. The block ends with NO full stop after `enemies`: the line runs to the extreme right margin of a leaf that loses ink there, and no stop is visible at 1600 dpi; the facing Latin ends `meis salvus ero.` with a stop. Transcribed as printed rather than repaired. The `d` of the earlier `name of the Lord.` has a damaged bowl but its stop is present.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: What return shall I make the Lord for all he has given to me? I will take the Chalice of salvation, and call upon the name of the Lord. Praising, I will call upon the Lord, and shall be saved from my enemies
Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quæ retribuit mihi? Calicem salutaris accipiam, et nomen Domini invocabo. Laudans invocabo Dominum, et ab inimicis meis salvus ero.

elements.note: Italic, centred on its own line across the full measure. `blood` lower case where the other rubrics of this page capitalise `Host` and `Chalice`.

translations.text: Receiving the blood of our Saviour, he says,

elements.name: Sanguis Domini nostri Jesu Christi
elements.note: `Amen.` italic in both columns. The English word order is `to everlasting life` here against `to life everlasting` at row 20, though the Latin is identical in both (`in vitam aeternam`).
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: The blood of our Lord Jesus Christ preserve my soul to everlasting life. Amen.
Sanguis Domini nostri Jesu Christi custodiat animam meam in vitam æternam. Amen.

elements.note: Italic, centred on its own line across the full measure. This is the last element on xlii before `Quod ore sumpsimus`, which begins directly beneath it and runs over onto xliii; that prayer belongs to the following lane and is not transcribed here.

translations.text: Taking the first Ablution, he says,

elements.name: Quod ore sumpsimus, Domine
elements.note: Runs over the page break at xlii/xliii; only the tail (`of a temporal gift ... remedy.`) stands on xliii, so this row overlaps the preceding lane, which owns xlii and the rubric `Taking the first Ablution, he says,` that heads the block. Scan damage on xlii: the first line prints `that wha` with only the top serif of the terminal t surviving at the right margin; read whole against the facing Latin `Quod ore sumpsimus`.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: Grant, Lord, that what we have taken with our mouth, we may receive with a pure mind, that of a temporal gift it may become to us an eternal remedy.
Quod ore sumpsimus, Domine, pura mente capiamus, et de munere temporali, fiat nobis remedium sempiternum.

elements.note: Italic, centred across the full measure above both columns.

translations.text: Taking the second Ablution, he says,

elements.name: Corpus tuum Domine, quod sumpsi
elements.note: `have drank` is the book's form. The conclusion is abbreviated `Who livest and reignest, &c.` where the Latin column sets it out in full, `Qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum. Amen.` Right margin clean on this leaf.
elements.speaker: priest

translations.text: May thy body, O Lord, which I have received, and thy blood which I have drank, cleave to my bowels; and grant, that no stain of sin may remain in me, who have been fed with this pure and holy sacrament. Who livest and reignest, &c.

Corpus tuum Domine, quod sumpsi, et sanguis quem potavi, adhæreat visceribus meis; et præsta ut in me non remaneat scelerum macula, quem pura et sancta refecerunt sacramenta. Qui vivis et regnas in sæcula sæculorum. Amen.
